newsitem.title: UK: Mideast tanker rates may rise on better fixing.
newsitem.headline: Mideast tanker rates may rise on better fixing.

text.p: Crude tanker chartering in the Middle East Gulf was good again on Thursday with rates on one of the key routes out of the region taking on an upwards bias.
Shipbrokers said that rates and fixing activity was looking better than seen over the last week and a half.
By mid afternoon, four VLCCs had been seen -- three finding employment to the East, and one to the U.S. Gulf.
The rate of W49 for Vela's chartering of the Berge Duke, travelling Middle East to the U.S. Gulf, was quite low and not seen to reflect the market, shipping brokers said.
They said VLCC trips to the East remained at W50.75 (though as high as W52 was seen), while vessels bound for Japan settled at last done levels of W56. No ULCC charters were reported.
"If this level of fixing activity is sustained it could support freight levels, so it genuinely looks as though rates will crawl slowly upwards," said one London broker.
Rates for 80,000 tonners going cross-Med slumped to W95, off W3 from last done, although as low as W90 and as high as W97.5 were seen, brokers said.
In the inter-UKC sector, rates settled at last done levels of W96, amid a dearth of fixtures.
By mid-afternoon, Esso's fixing of the 84,000 tonne Prospect, travelling cross UKC, was the only charter seen.

"Chartering activity has been poor on Thursday. The rates are not that high, so it isn't due to fear of high rates. There are plenty of vessels in the vicinity at the moment," said one Scandinavian broker. "It appears that charterers are holding back in the hope that rates drop further when other vessels become available."
Caribbean tankers saw rates, for 70,000 tonners making upcoast-U.S trips, remain on a plateau of W145. By mid-afternoon no charters had been seen.
